title: Spell cancellation doesn't call trackSentResponse(), causing spurious lost-callback-recovery
description:
After a spell is cancelled via `cancelSpellFromBadManaPlan()`, the bridge sends `session.sendPlayerBoolean(gameId, false)` but does not call `trackSentResponse()`. This leaves `lastResponseSentAt = 0`, so the lost callback recovery in `passPriority()` (line 3418) thinks no response was sent and fires a speculative pass after 10 seconds (STALL_NUDGE_MS).

In game_20260228_172012_g1, both post-cancellation timeouts for Gem25P Diplom (at 17:23:52 and 17:25:42) were directly caused by this — the bridge had already responded to the GAME_PLAY_MANA callback via cancellation, but the tracking state didn't reflect it.

Evidence:
- ~/.mage-bench/logs/game_20260228_172012_g1/Gem25P Diplom_mcp.log: lost callback recovery at 17:23:52 and 17:25:42, both immediately after SPELL_CANCELLED events

Source: BridgeCallbackHandler.java — cancelSpellFromBadManaPlan() (lines 5096-5110) calls sendPlayerBoolean but never trackSentResponse(). Compare with auto-response paths at lines 4437, 4445 which do call trackSentResponse().

Suggested fix: Add `trackSentResponse(gameId, ResponseType.BOOLEAN, false, null)` in cancelSpellFromBadManaPlan() after the sendPlayerBoolean call. This tells the recovery mechanism that a response was already sent, preventing the spurious 10-second nudge.
